nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 1: the blessed man and the way of the ungodly
nodes.d: The blessed man delights in the law of the LORD and is like a tree by streams of water, while the ungodly are like chaff and their way shall perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two ways in Psalm 1 and what the blessed man delights in?
ev: Contrast the tree and the chaff in Psalm 1 and say what each picture shows.

nodes.t: Psalm 2: the nations rage, the LORD’s king is set on Zion
nodes.d: The kings of the earth set themselves against the LORD and his anointed, the LORD laughs and says he has set his king on Zion, declares him his Son, and warns the kings to serve the LORD with fear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Psalm 2 in its four parts and say what the kings are warned to do?
ev: List who rages against whom (2:1-3), who answers (2:4-6), and what the kings are told to do (2:10-12).

nodes.t: Psalms 3-4: trusting the LORD and sleeping in peace
nodes.d: In Psalm 3 many rise up against the speaker but the LORD is a shield and he lies down and sleeps; in Psalm 4 he asks the LORD to hear him, says the LORD has put gladness in his heart, and lies down in peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the speaker of Psalms 3 and 4 is able to sleep despite trouble?
ev: Find the verse about sleep in each psalm (3:5, 4:8) and say what gives the speaker peace.

nodes.t: Psalms 5-7: prayers for help against enemies and for the LORD’s judgment
nodes.d: Psalm 5 is a morning prayer to a God who hates wickedness, Psalm 6 is a weary cry for mercy and healing, and Psalm 7 appeals to the LORD as righteous judge to save the speaker from persecutors.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how each of Psalms 5, 6 and 7 begins and what the speaker asks?
ev: Find the request in 5:8, the groaning in 6:6, and the appeal to God’s judgment in 7:8-9.

nodes.t: Psalm 8: what is man? the LORD’s majesty and man’s place
nodes.d: The speaker praises the LORD’s excellent name, considers the heavens, the moon and stars, and asks what man is that God remembers him, saying God made him a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory, with dominion over the works of his hands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 8:3-6 and say what it teaches about God and man?
ev: Read 8:3-8 and list what is put under man’s dominion.

nodes.t: Psalms 9-10: the LORD is a refuge for the oppressed and judges the wicked
nodes.d: Psalm 9 praises the LORD who sits on his throne judging, is a refuge for the oppressed and does not forget the cry of the humble; Psalm 10 asks why he stands afar and describes the wicked who persecute the poor, ending with the LORD hearing the humble.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalms 9 and 10 speak of the LORD as judge of the oppressor?
ev: List what the wicked say and do in Psalm 10:2-11, and the LORD’s response in 10:16-18.

nodes.t: Psalms 11-12: refuge when the faithful fail
nodes.d: Psalm 11 says the LORD is in his holy temple and trieth the righteous, and the speaker trusts him instead of fleeing; Psalm 12 says the godly cease and men speak flattery, but the words of the LORD are pure and he will arise for the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the speakers of Psalms 11 and 12 trust the LORD when evil seems strong?
ev: Read 11:1-4 and 12:5-6 and say why the speaker trusts the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 13: how long, O LORD?
nodes.d: The speaker asks how long the LORD will forget him and hide his face, pleads for light lest his enemy rejoice, and ends by trusting in the LORD’s mercy and singing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 13 moves from complaint to trust?
ev: Trace how the psalm moves from “how long” in 13:1-2 to singing in 13:5-6.

nodes.t: Psalms 14 and 53: the fool says there is no God
nodes.d: Both psalms say the fool has said in his heart there is no God, that the LORD looked down from heaven to see if any seek him, and that all are gone aside and none does good; the psalms end with a longing for the salvation of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Psalms 14 and 53 and say what they teach about human beings?
ev: Compare Psalm 14:1-3 and 53:1-3 and note the repeated words.
Find the closing wish in 14:7 and 53:6.

nodes.t: Psalm 15: who may dwell in the LORD’s tabernacle?
nodes.d: Asked who may abide in the LORD’s tabernacle and dwell in his holy hill, the psalm answers with the one who walks uprightly, speaks truth, does not slander or take usury or bribes, and honours those who fear the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list four qualities of the person described in Psalm 15?
ev: List the qualities named in 15:2-5.

nodes.t: Psalm 16: the LORD is my portion and I will not be moved
nodes.d: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD, calls him his portion and cup, sets him always before him, and expects his heart to be glad and his soul not left in hell, with fulness of joy and pleasures at God’s right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 16:8-11 about the LORD’s presence?
ev: Read 16:5-11 and list the reasons the speaker rejoices.

nodes.t: Psalm 17: hide me under the shadow of thy wings
nodes.d: The speaker appeals to the LORD to hear his right, says his heart has been tried and found without fault, asks to be kept as the apple of the eye from violent men, and expects to behold God’s face and be satisfied.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two pictures of God’s care in Psalm 17:8?
ev: Read 17:8-9 and 17:15 and say what the speaker asks and expects.

nodes.t: Psalm 18: the LORD my rock and deliverer; a king’s thanksgiving
nodes.d: The speaker loves the LORD as rock, fortress and deliverer, describes God coming down in storm and fire to rescue him from death and strong enemies, and gives thanks for strength in battle and for deliverance given to his king and anointed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 18 pictures the LORD rescuing the speaker?
ev: Read 18:1-6, 18:30-36 and 18:50 and list who delivers and who is delivered.

nodes.t: Psalm 19: the heavens declare God’s glory, and his law is perfect
nodes.d: The heavens declare the glory of God day and night to all the earth, and the law, testimony, statutes and judgments of the LORD are perfect, sure, right and sweeter than honey; the speaker asks to be cleansed from secret and presumptuous sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God makes himself known in Psalm 19 through the heavens and through his law?
ev: Read 19:1-6 and 19:7-11 and say what each half says about God.
Read 19:12-14 as a prayer.

nodes.t: Psalms 20-21: prayer and thanksgiving for the king
nodes.d: Psalm 20 prays that the LORD hear the king in the day of trouble and says some trust in chariots but we remember the name of the LORD; Psalm 21 thanks the LORD that the king rejoices in his salvation, with his heart’s desire and a crown.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast in Psalm 20:7 and who the king trusts in Psalm 21?
ev: Read 20:7 and 21:7 and say whom the king trusts.

nodes.t: Psalm 22: my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
nodes.d: The speaker cries to God who seems far, is scorned and surrounded by enemies, his bones out of joint and garments divided, then declares God’s name in the congregation and says all the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 22 moves from the opening cry to the closing praise?
ev: Read 22:1-21 and list the pictures of suffering.
Read 22:22-31 and say how the psalm ends.

nodes.t: Psalm 23: the LORD is my shepherd
nodes.d: The LORD is the speaker’s shepherd who leads him to green pastures and still waters, restores his soul, is with him in the valley of the shadow of death, prepares a table before enemies, and goodness and mercy follow him to the house of the LORD forever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for the speaker in Psalm 23 and where the psalm ends?
ev: List what the shepherd does in each verse of Psalm 23.

nodes.t: Psalm 24: the King of glory
nodes.d: The earth is the LORD’s and all in it; those with clean hands and a pure heart may ascend his hill, and the gates are told to lift up their heads for the King of glory, the LORD of hosts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who may stand in the LORD’s holy place and who the King of glory is in Psalm 24?
ev: Read 24:3-6 and say who may ascend, and 24:7-10 and say who comes in.

nodes.t: Psalm 25: teach me thy ways; forgive my sin
nodes.d: The speaker lifts up his soul to the LORD, asks to be taught his ways and truth, asks him not to remember his youthful sins and to pardon his great iniquity, and says the LORD teaches the meek and sinners in the way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the speaker asks for in Psalm 25 and whom the LORD teaches?
ev: Read 25:4-11 and list what the speaker asks for.
Read 25:8-14 and say whom the LORD teaches.

nodes.t: Psalm 26: examine me; I walk in my integrity
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD to judge and test him, says he walks in his truth, has not sat with vain persons, loves the LORD’s house, and asks not to be gathered with sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks God to do in Psalm 26:1-2?
ev: List what the speaker says he has done and not done in 26:3-8.

nodes.t: Psalm 27: the LORD is my light and salvation
nodes.d: The speaker says the LORD is his light, salvation and strength, so he will not fear though an army encamp against him; he desires to dwell in the LORD’s house, seeks his face, and says to wait on the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the speaker of Psalm 27 does not fear and what he asks for in 27:4?
ev: Read 27:1-6 and 27:13-14 and state what the speaker is confident about.
Read 27:4 and say what he most desires.

nodes.t: Psalms 28-29: the LORD my strength; the voice of the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 28 is a cry to the LORD the rock, then blessing him because he has heard and is the speaker’s strength and shield; Psalm 29 summons the mighty to give glory to the LORD whose voice is over the waters and shakes the wilderness, and who gives strength to his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three things the voice of the LORD does in Psalm 29?
ev: Find 28:7-8 and 29:11 and note how both speak of the LORD’s strength to his people.
List what the voice of the LORD does in 29:3-9.

nodes.t: Psalm 30: weeping may endure for a night
nodes.d: The speaker extols the LORD who lifted him up and healed him from the grave, says the LORD’s anger endures a moment but his favour is life, and that mourning was turned into dancing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 30:5 says about weeping and joy?
ev: Read 30:5 and 30:11-12 and say what changed.

nodes.t: Psalm 31: into thine hand I commit my spirit
nodes.d: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD as rock and fortress, commits his spirit into his hand, describes distress, reproach and fear on every side, says his times are in the LORD’s hand, and blesses him for his goodness laid up for those who fear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that “my times are in thy hand” in Psalm 31:15?
ev: Read 31:5, 31:15 and 31:19 and state what each says about trusting the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 32: blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven
nodes.d: The speaker says the one whose transgression is forgiven is blessed, describes bones wasting while he kept silent about his sin, and says that when he acknowledged his sin to the LORD he was forgiven and now the LORD is his hiding place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happens in Psalm 32:5 when the speaker confesses his sin?
ev: Contrast 32:3-4 with 32:5.
Read 32:1-2 and note who is called blessed.

nodes.t: Psalm 33: sing to the LORD who made all things by his word
nodes.d: The righteous are called to sing to the LORD a new song because his word is right and by his word the heavens were made; he looks on all men, brings counsel of nations to nought, and his eye is on those who fear him and hope in his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 33:6-9 says about creation by the LORD’s word?
ev: Read 33:6-9 and 33:16-19 and say how God’s word and rescue are described.

nodes.t: Psalm 34: taste and see that the LORD is good
nodes.d: The speaker blesses the LORD at all times, tells how this poor man cried and the LORD saved him, says the angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him, teaches children the fear of the LORD, and says the LORD is near the broken-hearted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Psalm 34 teaches about crying to the LORD and what children are taught in 34:11-14?
ev: Read 34:1-10 and 34:11-14 and list what the speaker teaches the children.

nodes.t: Psalm 35: plead my cause against false accusers
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD to contend with those who strive with him, to let the angel of the LORD chase them, and describes false witnesses who repay evil for good; he promises thanks in the great congregation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the wrong done to the speaker in Psalm 35 and what he asks of the LORD?
ev: Read 35:7, 35:11-12 and 35:18 and describe the wrong done to the speaker.

nodes.t: Psalm 36: the wicked and the fountain of life
nodes.d: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, while the LORD’s mercy reaches to the heavens and his faithfulness to the clouds; with him is the fountain of life and in his light we see light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast what Psalm 36 says about the wicked and about the LORD?
ev: Contrast 36:1-4 with 36:5-9.

nodes.t: Psalm 37: fret not, trust in the LORD
nodes.d: The psalm tells the reader not to fret over evildoers but to trust in the LORD, delight in him, commit his way to him and wait; the wicked will be cut off and the meek shall inherit the earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three commands in Psalm 37:1-8 and what is promised to the meek?
ev: Read 37:1-9 and list the commands given.
Read 37:25 and say what the speaker has observed.

nodes.t: Psalm 38: a penitent’s cry in suffering
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD not to rebuke him in wrath, says his flesh and bones suffer because of his sin and iniquity, his friends stand aloof and enemies speak against him, yet he hopes in the LORD and confesses his iniquity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the speaker of Psalm 38 connects his suffering to his sin and what he does about it?
ev: Read 38:1-4 and 38:15-18 and say what the speaker confesses and hopes.

nodes.t: Psalm 39: make me to know my end
nodes.d: The speaker resolves to guard his tongue, asks the LORD to make him know his end and how short his days are, calls man’s life an handbreadth, says his hope is in the LORD, and asks to be spared.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks God to teach him in Psalm 39:4-7?
ev: Read 39:4-7 and say what the speaker asks and what he concludes about his hope.

nodes.t: Psalm 40: I waited patiently for the LORD
nodes.d: The speaker waited patiently for the LORD who lifted him from a pit and put a new song in his mouth, says the LORD desires obedience and not sacrifice and offering, declares his righteousness to the congregation, and asks for help as poor and needy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 40:6-8 about sacrifice and the LORD’s will?
ev: Read 40:1-3 and 40:6-8 and say what the LORD desires according to the speaker.

nodes.t: Psalm 41: blessed is he that considers the poor
nodes.d: The one who considers the poor is blessed and the LORD delivers him in trouble; the speaker, ill and slandered by enemies and even a familiar friend, asks for mercy and the psalm ends with a blessing on the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what blessing Psalm 41:1-3 gives to the one who considers the poor?
ev: Read 41:1-3 and 41:9-13 and say who is blessed and who betrays the speaker.

nodes.t: Psalms 42-43: my soul thirsts for God; why art thou cast down?
nodes.d: The speaker pants after God like a deer after water, remembers going to God’s house, and three times asks his soul why it is cast down and tells it to hope in God; Psalm 43 asks God to plead his cause and lead him to his holy hill.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read the refrain of Psalms 42-43 and say what the speaker tells his soul?
ev: Find the repeated refrain (42:5, 42:11, 43:5) and say how the speaker answers his own soul.

nodes.t: Psalm 44: a lament of God’s people after defeat
nodes.d: The people recall what God did for their fathers in giving the land, say they trust not in their bow, but now God has cast them off, scattered them and made them a reproach though they have not forgotten him, and they ask him to awake and redeem them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the people complain in Psalm 44 and what they ask?
ev: Read 44:1-8, 44:9-16 and 44:17-26 and say what each section says.

nodes.t: Psalm 45: a song for the king
nodes.d: The speaker addresses a king who is fairer than the sons of men, whose throne is for ever and whose sceptre is righteous; he is anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows, and a king’s daughter is brought to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the king and his throne are praised in Psalm 45?
ev: Read 45:1-7 and say what is said about the king and 45:10-15 about the bride.

nodes.t: Psalm 46: God is our refuge and strength
nodes.d: God is a very present help in trouble, so the speakers will not fear though the earth is removed and the waters roar; God is in the midst of the city, the LORD of hosts is with us, and he makes wars cease and says, Be still, and know that I am God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 46:10 asks and why the speakers do not fear?
ev: Read 46:1-3, 46:4-7 and 46:8-11 and find the refrain in 46:7 and 46:11.

nodes.t: Psalms 47-48: God is king over all the earth; the city of God
nodes.d: Psalm 47 calls all peoples to clap and shout for God, who is the great King over all the earth; Psalm 48 praises the LORD in the city of our God on the mountain of Zion, where God is known as a refuge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalms 47 and 48 say about God as king and about Zion?
ev: Find 47:2, 47:7-8 and 48:1-3 and say what is said about God’s kingship and Zion.

nodes.t: Psalm 49: no man can redeem his brother; God will redeem my soul
nodes.d: The speaker calls all peoples to hear his wisdom and says those who trust in wealth cannot redeem a brother or give God a ransom, men die like beasts and carry nothing away, but God will redeem his soul from the grave.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says about riches and death in Psalm 49 and what he says God will do?
ev: Read 49:6-9 and 49:15 and contrast what riches cannot do with what God does.

nodes.t: Psalm 50: God judges his people; offer thanksgiving
nodes.d: God speaks from Zion to gather his saints who made a covenant with him by sacrifice, says he does not need bulls and goats, tells them to offer thanksgiving and call on him in trouble, and rebukes the wicked who hate instruction.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God says in Psalm 50:9-15 about sacrifice and thanksgiving?
ev: Read 50:7-15 and 50:16-23 and say what God asks and what he rebukes.

nodes.t: Psalm 51: have mercy upon me, O God
nodes.d: The speaker pleads for mercy and cleansing, confesses his transgression and says he sinned against God only, asks for a clean heart and a right spirit and that God not take his holy spirit, and says God desires a broken and contrite heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 51:10-12 and say what the speaker asks God to do?
ev: Read 51:1-4 and say what the speaker confesses.
Read 51:10-17 and list what he asks and what God accepts.

nodes.t: Psalms 52 and 54: God against the deceitful and violent
nodes.d: Psalm 52 asks why the mighty man boasts in mischief, says God will destroy the deceitful tongue, and compares the speaker to a green olive tree trusting in God’s mercy; Psalm 54 asks God to save him from strangers and oppressors and says God is his helper.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the man in Psalm 52:7 with the speaker in 52:8?
ev: Compare what the boaster trusts (52:7) with what the speaker trusts (52:8).

nodes.t: Psalm 55: betrayed by an equal, cast thy burden on the LORD
nodes.d: The speaker is overwhelmed by fear and wishes he had wings to flee, sees violence in the city, is wounded not by an enemy but by an equal and familiar friend, and resolves to pray evening, morning and noon, trusting that God will hear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does in Psalm 55:16-17 and who has caused his grief in 55:12-14?
ev: Read 55:12-14 and 55:16-22 and say who wounds the speaker and what he does.

nodes.t: Psalms 56-57: in God I will trust and not be afraid
nodes.d: In Psalm 56 the speaker says that when afraid he will trust in God and not fear what man can do; in Psalm 57 he takes refuge in the shadow of God’s wings and says his heart is fixed to sing, asking God to be exalted above the heavens.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does when afraid in Psalm 56:3-4?
ev: Find 56:3-4, 56:11 and 57:1, 57:7 and say what the speaker does when afraid.

nodes.t: Psalms 58-59: God judges unjust rulers and rescues from violent men
nodes.d: Psalm 58 asks whether the congregation judges uprightly and appeals to God to break the teeth of the wicked, concluding that there is a God who judges in the earth; Psalm 59 asks God to deliver from bloodthirsty enemies and sings of his strength and mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalms 58 and 59 end and what each says about God?
ev: Read 58:11 and 59:16-17 and say how each psalm ends.

nodes.t: Psalm 60: a prayer after a defeat
nodes.d: The speaker says God has cast off and scattered his people and made them drink the wine of astonishment, prays for deliverance, recalls God’s claim on Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim and Judah, and says vain is the help of man while through God we shall do valiantly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 60:11-12 says about help from man and from God?
ev: Read 60:1-5 and 60:11-12 and say what the people ask and trust.

nodes.t: Psalms 61-62: my rock and my refuge; wait on God alone
nodes.d: In Psalm 61 the speaker cries from the end of the earth and asks to be led to a rock higher than he, a strong tower; in Psalm 62 his soul waits on God alone, his rock and salvation, and he says power belongs to God and mercy belongs to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the names for God in Psalm 62:1-8 and say what the speaker does?
ev: Find 61:2-3 and 62:1-2, 62:5-8 and list the names for God.

nodes.t: Psalm 63: my soul thirsts for thee
nodes.d: The speaker earnestly seeks God in a dry and thirsty land, says God’s lovingkindness is better than life, remembers him on his bed in the night watches, and says his soul follows hard after God and the king shall rejoice in God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 63:3 says about God’s lovingkindness?
ev: Read 63:1-8 and list the ways the speaker seeks and praises God.

nodes.t: Psalm 64: hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked
nodes.d: The speaker asks God to preserve his life from enemies who sharpen their tongues like swords and shoot bitter words and plan snares in secret; God shall shoot at them and all men shall fear and declare his work.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the wicked do and what God does in Psalm 64?
ev: Read 64:3-6 and 64:7-10 and contrast the wicked’s weapons with God’s.

nodes.t: Psalms 65-67: praise for God’s forgiveness, creation and blessing of the nations
nodes.d: Psalm 65 says praise waits for God who purges transgressions and waters the earth and crowns the year with goodness; Psalm 66 calls all lands to praise him for his works and for bringing his people through trial; Psalm 67 asks God to bless us so that all the earth may fear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the refrain of Psalm 67:3 and 67:5 asks of all the peoples?
ev: Find 65:3, 65:9-13, 66:5-12 and 67:1-3 and list what is praised.

nodes.t: Psalm 68: let God arise
nodes.d: The psalm begins with Let God arise and his enemies be scattered, calls God a father of the fatherless and judge of the widows who leads his people, and calls the kingdoms of the earth to sing to God who rides on the heavens.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 68:5-6 says about God’s care for the weak?
ev: Read 68:1-6 and 68:32-35 and note who is called to rejoice and sing.

nodes.t: Psalm 69: zeal for thy house; they gave me vinegar
nodes.d: The speaker is sinking in deep waters and hated without cause, says zeal for God’s house has consumed him and reproaches have fallen on him, that he was given gall and vinegar, asks that his adversaries’ table be a snare and their eyes darkened, and ends with praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the suffering in Psalm 69:1-4 and 69:20-21 and how the psalm ends?
ev: Read 69:1-4, 69:9, 69:21 and 69:22-28 and list what the speaker suffers and asks.

nodes.t: Psalms 70-71: make haste to help; forsake me not in old age
nodes.d: Psalm 70 is a short cry for God to hasten and help the poor and needy speaker; Psalm 71 trusts in God from youth, asks not to be cast off in old age, and promises to declare God’s righteousness and strength to the next generation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks of God in old age in Psalm 71:9 and 71:18?
ev: Read 71:5-9 and 71:17-18 and say what the speaker asks and promises.

nodes.t: Psalm 72: the king who judges the poor with righteousness
nodes.d: The psalm prays that God give the king his judgments and righteousness so that he judges the poor, saves the needy, and breaks the oppressor, that his dominion be from sea to sea and his name endure, and all nations be blessed in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what kind of king Psalm 72 describes and how he treats the poor?
ev: Read 72:1-4, 72:12-14 and 72:17-19 and list what the king does for the poor.

nodes.t: Psalm 73: why the wicked prosper; I went into the sanctuary
nodes.d: The speaker nearly slipped because he envied the prosperity of the wicked and thought cleansing his heart was in vain, until he went into God’s sanctuary and understood their end; he says God is the strength of his heart and his portion and it is good to draw near to God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what changed the speaker’s mind in Psalm 73:16-17?
ev: Read 73:1-14 and 73:15-20 and say what changed his view.

nodes.t: Psalm 74: a lament over the destroyed sanctuary
nodes.d: The people ask why God has cast them off for ever, describe the enemy wrecking the sanctuary and burning the meeting places, say there is no prophet, recall God’s power in creation and dividing the sea, and ask him to plead his cause.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the people recall creation and the sea in Psalm 74:12-17?
ev: Read 74:1-11 and 74:12-17 and say how remembering God’s past works shapes the plea.

nodes.t: Psalms 75-76: God is the judge; God is known in Judah
nodes.d: In Psalm 75 the speaker gives thanks to God and says he judges uprightly, puts down one and sets up another, and warns the boastful; Psalm 76 says God is known in Judah, his dwelling is in Zion, and he breaks the weapons and rebukes the proud.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 75:6-7 says about who raises and who puts down?
ev: Read 75:6-8 and 76:1-3 and say who judges and where he is known.

nodes.t: Psalm 77: I will remember the works of the LORD
nodes.d: In trouble the speaker cries to God and asks whether he has cast off for ever and forgotten to be gracious; then he resolves to remember the works and wonders of the LORD, who led his people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker does in Psalm 77:10-12 when he feels God has forgotten him?
ev: Read 77:7-9 and 77:10-20 and trace the turn from questions to remembering.

nodes.t: Psalm 78: tell the coming generation what God did and how Israel rebelled
nodes.d: The speaker says the fathers must teach their children the LORD’s works so they will not be stubborn like their fathers; he retells Egypt, the sea, the wilderness provision and Israel’s repeated unbelief, God’s anger, and his choosing of Judah, Zion and David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the psalmist retells Israel’s history in Psalm 78:1-8 and what repeated pattern follows?
ev: Read 78:1-8 and say why the story is told.
Trace the cycle of provision, rebellion and judgment in 78:12-64.

nodes.t: Psalms 79-80: pleas for Jerusalem and the vine of Israel
nodes.d: Psalm 79 laments that the nations have defiled God’s temple and shed blood in Jerusalem and asks God not to remember former iniquities but to help for his name’s sake; Psalm 80 prays that the Shepherd of Israel turn us again, picturing Israel as a vine brought out of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the vine picture in Psalm 80 and what the people ask in the refrain?
ev: Find the refrain in 80:3, 80:7, 80:19 and the vine imagery in 80:8-16.

nodes.t: Psalms 81-82: hear my people; God judges among the gods
nodes.d: Psalm 81 calls Israel to sing and recalls the LORD who brought them from Egypt, who asks them to listen and says he would have fed them had they obeyed; Psalm 82 shows God standing in the congregation to judge those who judge unjustly and favour the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God says in Psalm 81:8-13 and what he says to the judges in Psalm 82:2-4?
ev: Read 81:8-16 and 82:1-4 and say what God asks and rebukes.

nodes.t: Psalm 83: a plea against nations conspiring against God’s people
nodes.d: The speaker says God’s enemies make a tumult and consult together against his people, names Edom, Moab, Ammon, Assur and others, asks God to deal with them as with Midian and Sisera, so that they may know that he alone is the most high over all the earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the plan of the enemies in Psalm 83:3-5 and what the speaker hopes people will know?
ev: Read 83:1-8 and 83:16-18 and say what the enemies plan and what the speaker asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 84: how amiable are thy tabernacles
nodes.d: The speaker longs for the courts of the LORD, says the sparrow finds a house near his altars, blesses those whose strength is in God and who pass through the valley of Baca, and says a day in his courts is better than a thousand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 84:10 says about being in God’s house?
ev: Read 84:1-4 and 84:10-12 and say what the speaker values.

nodes.t: Psalm 85: revive us; mercy and truth meet
nodes.d: The people thank the LORD for favour and forgiveness to the land, ask him to turn them again and revive them, and say mercy and truth are met together, righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 85:10-11 says about mercy, truth, righteousness and peace?
ev: Read 85:1-7 and 85:8-13 and say what the speaker expects God to speak.

nodes.t: Psalm 86: unite my heart to fear thy name
nodes.d: The speaker, poor and needy, asks the LORD to hear and preserve him, says the Lord is good and ready to forgive and there is none like him among the gods, asks to be taught his way and for a united heart, and says God is full of compassion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker asks in Psalm 86:11 and what he says about God in 86:15?
ev: Read 86:5, 86:8-11 and 86:15 and list what is said about God.

nodes.t: Psalm 87: glorious things are spoken of Zion
nodes.d: The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob, glorious things are spoken of the city of God, and the LORD records of peoples that this one was born there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 87 says about Zion and about the nations?
ev: Read 87:1-7 and list what is said about Zion and who is counted as born there.

nodes.t: Psalm 88: a cry from the depths with no answer in sight
nodes.d: The speaker is full of troubles, near the grave, afflicted by God’s wrath and forsaken by friends, and cries to the LORD day and night; the psalm ends in darkness without a stated answer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 88 begins and why its ending is different from Psalm 13?
ev: Read 88:1-4 and 88:13-18 and note how the psalm begins and ends.

nodes.t: Psalm 89: the LORD’s covenant with David
nodes.d: The psalm sings of the LORD’s mercies and faithfulness, says he made a covenant with his chosen David and swore to establish his seed and throne for ever, then laments that the LORD has cast off and abhorred his anointed and asks him to remember.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised David in Psalm 89 and what the psalmist complains about at the end?
ev: Read 89:3-4, 89:28-37 and 89:38-45 and contrast the promise with the lament.

nodes.t: Psalm 90: teach us to number our days
nodes.d: The speaker says the LORD has been our dwelling place in all generations and is God from everlasting, while man is like grass and a thousand years are as yesterday; he asks to be taught to number his days, to be satisfied with mercy, and for the work of their hands to be established.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 90:12 asks God to teach and why?
ev: Read 90:1-6 and 90:12-17 and contrast God’s time with man’s.

nodes.t: Psalm 91: he that dwells in the secret place of the most High
nodes.d: The one who dwells in the secret place of the most High abides under the shadow of the Almighty, who is his refuge and fortress; he will not fear the terror by night or the arrow by day, God gives his angels charge over him, and the LORD speaks of delivering him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 91:1-2 says about the person who trusts in the LORD?
ev: Read 91:1-2 and 91:14-16 and list what the one who trusts receives.

nodes.t: Psalms 92-93: it is good to give thanks; the LORD reigns
nodes.d: Psalm 92 says it is good to give thanks to the LORD and praise his works, that the righteous flourish like a palm tree and bring forth fruit in old age; Psalm 93 declares that the LORD reigns, clothed with majesty and strength, his throne established of old.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the righteous in Psalm 92:12-14 and the opening of Psalm 93?
ev: Read 92:12-15 and 93:1-4 and say what is said about the righteous and about the LORD’s reign.

nodes.t: Psalm 94: O LORD God, to whom vengeance belongeth
nodes.d: The speaker calls on God as judge of the earth to reward the proud, asks how long the wicked will triumph and kill the widow and fatherless, says the LORD who made the ear hears and he will not cast off his people, and the LORD is his defence.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 94:9 and 94:14?
ev: Read 94:1-7 and 94:8-15 and 94:16-23 and say what the speaker asks and what he trusts.

nodes.t: Psalm 95: come, let us worship; harden not your heart
nodes.d: The psalm calls the people to sing to the LORD, the great King above all gods, who made the sea and dry land and is our shepherd; then it warns not to harden the heart as in the wilderness at Meribah, where God swore they should not enter his rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two parts of Psalm 95 and what the people are warned not to do?
ev: Read 95:1-7 and 95:8-11 and say what the call to worship and the warning each ask.

nodes.t: Psalms 96-99: the LORD reigns over all the earth
nodes.d: These psalms call the earth to sing a new song to the LORD, say all the gods of the nations are idols but the LORD made the heavens, repeat that the LORD reigns, and call the world to exalt him as holy and to rejoice at his coming to judge in righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalms 96-99 say about the LORD’s reign and the gods of the nations?
ev: Find the phrase “the LORD reigneth” in 96:10, 97:1 and 99:1, and say what each psalm adds.

nodes.t: Psalm 100: make a joyful noise unto the LORD
nodes.d: All lands are called to serve the LORD with gladness, know that he made us and we are his people and the sheep of his pasture, and enter his gates with thanksgiving because he is good and his mercy is everlasting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Psalm 100 says to give thanks to the LORD?
ev: Read Psalm 100 and list the reasons given for thanks.

nodes.t: Psalm 101: I will walk within my house with a perfect heart
nodes.d: The speaker resolves to sing of mercy and judgment, to behave wisely in a perfect way, to set no wicked thing before his eyes, to cut off the slanderer and proud, and to look to the faithful of the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three things the speaker of Psalm 101 resolves to do or not to do?
ev: List the resolutions in 101:2-8.

nodes.t: Psalm 102: the afflicted pours out his complaint; thou art the same
nodes.d: The afflicted speaker says his days are consumed like smoke and his bones cleave to his skin, he is like a pelican of the wilderness and a sparrow alone, but the LORD shall endure for ever, will build up Zion and hear the destitute, and the heavens will perish while he remains.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the speaker’s condition with the LORD’s endurance in Psalm 102?
ev: Read 102:1-11 and 102:12-22 and 102:23-28 and contrast the speaker with the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 103: bless the LORD, O my soul
nodes.d: The speaker tells his soul to bless the LORD and forget not his benefits: forgiveness, healing, redemption; the LORD is merciful, gracious and slow to anger, removes our transgressions as far as east from west, pities like a father, and knows we are dust.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the LORD’s benefits in Psalm 103 and read 103:8-12?
ev: List the benefits in 103:3-5 and the character of the LORD in 103:8-14.

nodes.t: Psalm 104: the LORD’s creation and provision
nodes.d: The speaker blesses the LORD for stretching out the heavens, setting the earth’s foundations, sending springs and grass for the cattle, giving the beasts and birds their places, and says all creatures look to him for food and live when he sends his spirit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 104 says about God’s care for creation and every creature?
ev: Read 104:1-9, 104:10-23 and 104:24-30 and list what the LORD provides.

nodes.t: Psalm 105: remember his wonderful works and his covenant with Abraham
nodes.d: The psalm calls Israel to give thanks and remember the LORD’s works, recounts his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give them Canaan, Joseph sent before them, the plagues of Egypt, and the exodus and wilderness provision, so that they might keep his statutes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list four events recounted in Psalm 105 and say why they are told?
ev: Read 105:7-11 and 105:23-45 and list the events retold.

nodes.t: Psalm 106: our fathers sinned; he remembered his covenant
nodes.d: The psalm confesses that the fathers sinned at the Red Sea, in the wilderness with the golden calf, at Baal-peor and at Meribah, and in Canaan among the heathen, yet God heard their cry and remembered his covenant; the speaker asks him to gather them from the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 106 differs from Psalm 105 in how it tells Israel’s history?
ev: Read 106:6-7 and 106:44-48 and list the sins confessed in 106:13-39.

nodes.t: Psalm 107: let the redeemed of the LORD say so
nodes.d: The redeemed are told to give thanks for the LORD’s goodness; four groups are described, wanderers in the wilderness, prisoners, the sick, and sailors in a storm, each cried to the LORD in trouble and he delivered them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the four groups in Psalm 107 and the refrain that follows each?
ev: List the four groups and find the repeated refrain (107:8, 15, 21, 31).

nodes.t: Psalm 108: awake, psaltery and harp
nodes.d: The speaker resolves to sing and praise, says God’s mercy is great above the heavens, and asks for help against the enemy using words that also appear in Psalm 60:5-12 about Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah and Edom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Psalm 108 with Psalm 57 and Psalm 60 and say which verses are alike?
ev: Compare Psalm 108:6-13 with 60:5-12 and note the shared words.

nodes.t: Psalm 109: a cry against false accusers
nodes.d: The speaker says the wicked speak against him with lying tongues and repay evil for love, and prays that the accuser’s days be few and his reward come from the LORD; he says he is poor and needy and asks God to save him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 109 moves from the speaker’s complaint to his prayer for help?
ev: Read 109:1-5, 109:6-20 and 109:21-31 and note how the psalm moves from complaint to curse to appeal.

nodes.t: Psalm 110: sit at my right hand; a priest after Melchizedek
nodes.d: The LORD says to the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool; he is a king sent to rule from Zion and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 110:1 and 110:4 and say what the LORD says to the speaker’s Lord?
ev: Read 110:1-4 and say who speaks and to whom, and what is sworn.

nodes.t: Psalms 111-112: the works of the LORD and the blessed man who fears him
nodes.d: Psalm 111 praises the LORD’s works, righteousness and covenant, saying the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; Psalm 112 describes the man who fears the LORD and delights in his commandments, whose righteousness endures and who is gracious and gives to the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 111:10 and Psalm 112:1 connect the fear of the LORD with wisdom and blessing?
ev: Read 111:10 and 112:1-9 and say what each says about the fear of the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalms 113-114: the LORD lifts the poor; the sea saw it and fled
nodes.d: Psalm 113 calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name, says he dwells on high yet humbles himself and raises the poor from the dust; Psalm 114 recalls Israel leaving Egypt when the sea fled and Jordan turned back and the earth trembled before the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 113:7-8 says about the poor and what Psalm 114 recalls?
ev: Read 113:5-9 and 114:1-8 and say what the LORD does in each.

nodes.t: Psalm 115: not unto us; idols and the living God
nodes.d: The psalm gives glory to the LORD’s name, says the heathen’s idols have mouths that speak not and eyes that see not and those who trust them become like them, and calls Israel, the house of Aaron and all who fear him to trust the LORD, their help and shield.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the idols with the LORD in Psalm 115?
ev: Read 115:4-8 and 115:9-11 and contrast idols with the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 116: I love the LORD because he heard my voice
nodes.d: The speaker loves the LORD because he heard his voice, tells how the sorrows of death compassed him and he called on the LORD who delivered his soul, and asks what he can render, promising to take the cup of salvation and pay his vows in the presence of all his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker promises to do in Psalm 116:12-14?
ev: Read 116:3-4 and 116:12-19 and say what the speaker does in thanks.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:1-32: blessed are those who walk in the law of the LORD
nodes.d: The psalm opens by calling blessed those who walk in the LORD’s law, asks how a young man may cleanse his way and says he has hid God’s word in his heart, and asks the LORD to open his eyes to see wondrous things out of his law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Psalm 119:9-11 and name three words the psalm uses for God’s word?
ev: Read 119:9-11 and say how a young man is to cleanse his way.
List the different words for God’s word used in 119:1-32.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:33-64: teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD to teach him his statutes, turn his eyes from vanity, and let his mercies come; he says he will speak of the LORD’s testimonies before kings, is the LORD’s portion, and has turned his feet to the LORD’s testimonies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the speaker asks God to teach and turn away in Psalm 119:33-40?
ev: Pick three requests the speaker makes in 119:33-40.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:65-96: it is good for me that I have been afflicted
nodes.d: The speaker says that before he was afflicted he went astray but now keeps God’s word, that it is good for him to have been afflicted that he might learn the statutes, that God’s hands made him, and that God’s word is settled for ever in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 119:67 and 119:71 say about affliction?
ev: Read 119:67, 119:71, 119:75 and 119:89 and say what the speaker has learned through affliction.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:97-128: O how I love thy law; thy word is a lamp unto my feet
nodes.d: The speaker loves God’s law and meditates on it all day, says it makes him wiser than his enemies and teachers, calls God’s words sweeter than honey, and says the word is a lamp unto his feet and a light unto his path.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 119:105 and explain what it says the word does?
ev: Read 119:97-105 and say what the speaker says the law gives him.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:129-160: the entrance of thy words giveth light
nodes.d: The speaker says God’s testimonies are wonderful and his words give light and understanding, weeps because others do not keep the law, asks to be redeemed from oppression, and says the sum of God’s word is truth and every righteous judgment endures for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 119:130 and 119:160 say about God’s word?
ev: Read 119:129-136 and 119:160 and say what the speaker says about God’s word.

nodes.t: Psalm 119:161-176: great peace have they which love thy law
nodes.d: The speaker says princes persecute him without cause but his heart stands in awe of God’s word, he rejoices at it as one who finds great spoil, praises God seven times a day, says great peace have they that love the law, and ends by asking to be sought as a lost sheep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 119 ends and what the speaker asks in verse 176?
ev: Read 119:161-168 and 119:176 and say how the psalm ends.

nodes.t: Psalms 120-121: distress among liars; my help comes from the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 120 cries to the LORD in distress against lying lips and a deceitful tongue, among those who hate peace; Psalm 121 lifts the eyes to the hills and says help comes from the LORD who made heaven and earth and who keeps his people and never slumbers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 121 says about who keeps the speaker and when?
ev: Read 121:1-8 and list what the LORD keeps and when.

nodes.t: Psalm 122: I was glad when they said, let us go to the house of the LORD
nodes.d: The speaker is glad to go up to the house of the LORD to Jerusalem, where the tribes go up and the thrones of the house of David are set, and asks others to pray for the peace of Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Psalm 122:6-9 asks and why?
ev: Read 122:1-9 and list the reasons to love Jerusalem.

nodes.t: Psalms 123-125: our eyes wait upon the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 123 lifts eyes like servants watching a master’s hand and asks for mercy against contempt; Psalm 124 says that if the LORD had not been on our side the proud waters would have gone over us; Psalm 125 says those who trust in the LORD are like mount Zion, which cannot be removed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain one picture each from Psalms 123, 124 and 125?
ev: Find the pictures in 123:2, 124:7 and 125:1-2.

nodes.t: Psalm 126: they that sow in tears shall reap in joy
nodes.d: The people recall the LORD turning again the captivity of Zion when they were like those who dream, filled with laughter, and pray for the LORD to turn their captivity again, saying those who sow in tears shall reap in joy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of sowing in tears and reaping in joy in Psalm 126:5-6?
ev: Read 126:5-6 and say what the sower does and receives.

nodes.t: Psalms 127-128: unless the LORD builds the house; the blessed family
nodes.d: Psalm 127 says that unless the LORD builds the house those who build it labour in vain, and that children are a heritage from the LORD; Psalm 128 blesses the one who fears the LORD with the fruit of his labour, a fruitful wife and children, and the good of Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 127:1 teaches about work and the LORD?
ev: Read 127:1-2 and 128:1-4 and say what depends on the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 129: they have afflicted me from my youth, yet have not prevailed
nodes.d: Israel says they have often been afflicted from their youth yet not overcome, the LORD is righteous and has cut asunder the cords of the wicked, and those who hate Zion are compared to grass on the housetops that withers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 129:2-4 says about the afflicted and the LORD?
ev: Read 129:1-4 and say why the afflicted have not been overcome.

nodes.t: Psalms 130-131: out of the depths; a weaned child
nodes.d: Psalm 130 cries to the LORD out of the depths, says that with him there is forgiveness and plenteous redemption, and waits for him more than watchmen for the morning; Psalm 131 says the speaker is not haughty and has quieted his soul like a weaned child, and both end by telling Israel to hope in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 130:3-4 says about forgiveness and what 130:7 and 131:3 tell Israel to do?
ev: Read 130:3-8 and 131:1-3 and say what Israel is told to do.

nodes.t: Psalm 132: the LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion
nodes.d: The psalm recalls David’s vow to find a dwelling for the LORD and says the LORD swore to David that his seed would sit on his throne if his children keep his covenant; the LORD chose Zion for his rest and will make the horn of David to bud.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 132:11-12 says the LORD swore to David?
ev: Read 132:11-18 and say what the LORD swore and what he chose.

nodes.t: Psalms 133-134: brethren in unity; bless the LORD in the night
nodes.d: Psalm 133 says it is good and pleasant when brethren dwell together in unity, like precious ointment and the dew of Hermon, for there the LORD commands the blessing; Psalm 134 calls the LORD’s servants who stand in his house by night to lift up their hands and bless him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 133:1 says is good and what Psalm 134 calls the servants to do?
ev: Read 133:1-3 and 134:1-3 and say who is called to do what.

nodes.t: Psalm 135: praise the LORD who is great above all gods
nodes.d: The psalm calls the LORD’s servants to praise him, says he is above all gods and does whatever he pleases in heaven and earth, recalls Egypt’s firstborn and the defeat of Sihon and Og, and says those who make idols become like them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 135 contrasts the LORD with idols?
ev: Read 135:5-14 and 135:15-18 and list what the LORD does and what idols are.

nodes.t: Psalm 136: his mercy endureth for ever
nodes.d: Each verse tells a work of the LORD, from creation of the heavens and lights to the striking of Egypt’s firstborn, the dividing of the Red Sea and the giving of the land, and each is followed by the refrain that his mercy endures for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three works of the LORD in Psalm 136 and say the refrain?
ev: Read Psalm 136 and list the works named, noting the repeated refrain.

nodes.t: Psalm 137: by the rivers of Babylon
nodes.d: Exiles sit by the rivers of Babylon and weep when they remember Zion, hang up their harps when their captors ask for a song, and vow not to forget Jerusalem; the psalm ends with a plea against Babylon and Edom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the exiles in Psalm 137 will not sing and what they vow about Jerusalem?
ev: Read 137:1-6 and say what the exiles refuse to do and what they promise.

nodes.t: Psalm 138: I will praise thee with my whole heart
nodes.d: The speaker praises the LORD for his lovingkindness and truth, for answering when he cried, says kings shall sing of the LORD and that though he is high he regards the lowly, and says the LORD will perfect that which concerns him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 138:6-8 about God and the lowly?
ev: Read 138:1-8 and say what the speaker praises God for.

nodes.t: Psalm 139: O LORD, thou hast searched me and known me
nodes.d: The speaker says the LORD knows his sitting and rising and thoughts, that he cannot flee from his presence in heaven, the depths or the uttermost sea, that God formed him in the womb so that he is fearfully and wonderfully made, and asks God to search him and lead him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 139 says about God’s knowledge of us and his presence?
ev: Read 139:1-6, 139:7-12 and 139:13-16 and say what each part says about God.
Read 139:23-24 as a prayer.

nodes.t: Psalms 140-142: deliver me from violent men; I cried unto the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 140 asks the LORD to deliver the speaker from evil and violent men whose tongues are like serpents; Psalm 141 asks that his prayer be set before the LORD like incense and that he be kept from wickedness; Psalm 142 pours out his complaint, saying the LORD is his refuge and portion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 141:2-4 and 142:5 say about the speaker’s prayer and refuge?
ev: Read 140:1-3, 141:1-4 and 142:1-7 and list what the speaker asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 143: enter not into judgment with thy servant
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD to hear and not to enter into judgment with him since in God’s sight no man living is righteous, remembers the days of old, spreads out his hands, and asks to be taught to do God’s will and led into the land of uprightness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 143:2 says about being righteous in God’s sight?
ev: Read 143:1-2 and 143:8-10 and list what the speaker asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 144: blessed be the LORD my strength; happy is that people
nodes.d: The speaker blesses the LORD who teaches his hands to war and is his fortress and deliverer, asks what man is that God takes knowledge of him, asks for rescue from false and strange children, and describes the happy people whose God is the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 144:15 says makes a people happy?
ev: Read 144:1-4 and 144:12-15 and list the names for God and the picture of the happy people.

nodes.t: Psalm 145: I will extol thee, my God, O King
nodes.d: The speaker will bless the LORD every day and speak of his greatness, calls him gracious, full of compassion, slow to anger, good to all, near to all who call on him, upholding the fallen, and says his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 145:8-9 and name three things it says about the LORD?
ev: Read 145:8-9 and 145:13-20 and list what is said about God’s character and care.

nodes.t: Psalms 146-148: praise the LORD from the heavens and the earth
nodes.d: Psalm 146 says to praise the LORD all one’s life and not to trust in princes, since the LORD gives justice and feeds the hungry; Psalm 147 praises him for rebuilding Jerusalem, healing the broken-hearted and his word on the earth; Psalm 148 calls angels, the sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, mountains and kings to praise him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list five things called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148?
ev: List what is called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148 and what the LORD does in 146:7-9.

nodes.t: Psalms 149-150: let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 149 calls the saints to sing a new song to the LORD with dancing and swords in their hands; Psalm 150 closes the book by calling for praise of God in his sanctuary and firmament with trumpet, harp, cymbals and all that has breath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 150 and say who is to praise the LORD and with what?
ev: Read Psalm 150 and list where, why and with what God is to be praised.

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: The temptation in the wilderness
nodes.d: After forty days of fasting Jesus is tempted three times by the devil and answers each with “it is written”; the devil leaves and angels minister to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the devil offered Jesus and how Jesus replied?
ev: List the three temptations
Say what Jesus answered each time

nodes.t: The mustard seed and the leaven
nodes.d: Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a tiny mustard seed that becomes a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal, and Matthew says he spoke only in parables to the crowd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the mustard seed and leaven parables and what they say about the kingdom?
ev: Retell the two parables
Say what Matthew says in 13:34-35

nodes.t: Jesus enters Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for an ass and colt, and rides toward Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and branches and cry Hosanna to the son of David; Matthew says this fulfils a word about the King coming meek on an ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus came into Jerusalem and what the crowds said?
ev: Describe the entry
Say what the crowds shouted

nodes.t: Cleansing the temple
nodes.d: Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, overturns tables and seats, says the house of prayer has become a den of thieves, heals the blind and lame, and answers the priests about children’s praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus overturned the tables?
ev: Say what Jesus did and quoted
Describe what the children cried and the priests’ reaction

nodes.t: The parable of the wicked tenants
nodes.d: Tenants of a vineyard beat and kill the owner’s servants and then his son; Jesus cites the rejected stone made head of the corner, says the kingdom will be taken from them, and the priests perceive he speaks of them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and tenants stand for in the parable?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the priests understood

nodes.t: David’s son and David’s Lord
nodes.d: Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son Christ is; they say David’s, and he asks how David in spirit calls him Lord; no one can answer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the puzzle Jesus raised about David and the Christ?
ev: Retell the question Jesus asked
Say what the Pharisees could not answer

nodes.t: The mocking and crucifixion
nodes.d: Soldiers mock Jesus with a robe and thorns, Simon of Cyrene carries his cross, he is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves under the title King of the Jews, and passers-by taunt him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was mocked and crucified?
ev: Describe the mocking
List the details of the crucifixion

nodes.t: The death of Jesus
nodes.d: Darkness covers the land, Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and yields up the ghost; the temple veil tears, the earth quakes, graves open, and the centurion says truly this was the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs at his death
Say what the centurion said

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: The entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt that no one has ridden; he rides it as people spread garments and branches and shout Hosanna, blessing him that comes in the name of the Lord and the kingdom of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus entered Jerusalem?
ev: Retell how the colt was found
Say what the people shouted

nodes.t: The parable of the vineyard tenants
nodes.d: A man plants a vineyard and lets it to husbandmen who beat and kill his servants and then his beloved son; Jesus cites the rejected stone that became head of the corner, and the rulers know the parable is against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and husbandmen stand for?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the rulers understood

nodes.t: David’s Lord and warning against the scribes
nodes.d: Teaching in the temple, Jesus asks how the Christ can be David’s son when David calls him Lord, and warns the people against scribes who love honour and devour widows’ houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus asked about David and the Christ?
ev: State the puzzle Jesus raised about David
List what he warns about the scribes

nodes.t: The mocking and crucifixion
nodes.d: Soldiers dress Jesus in purple and a crown of thorns and mock him; Simon of Cyrene carries his cross; he is crucified at Golgotha between two thieves under the title King of the Jews while others mock.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was crucified?
ev: Describe the mockery
List what is said of the crucifixion

nodes.t: The death of Jesus
nodes.d: Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and dies; the temple veil tears, and the centurion says truly this man was the Son of God; women watch from afar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs and the centurion’s words
Name the women who watched

nodes.t: Luke: The Gospel Orderly Told
nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.t: The Temptation in the Wilderness
nodes.d: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is tempted forty days by the devil and answers each of three temptations with 'It is written' and a word of Scripture; the devil departs for a season.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the three temptations and how Jesus answered them?
ev: Name the three temptations and how Jesus answered each.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt, rides it toward Jerusalem as the disciples spread clothes and praise God, saying 'Blessed be the King that cometh', and weeps over the city that does not know the things of its peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry to Jerusalem and why he wept?
ev: Retell the entry and say why Jesus wept over Jerusalem.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
nodes.d: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants are beaten and sent away and whose beloved son is killed by the tenants; he says the owner will destroy them and give the vineyard to others, and cites the rejected stone that becomes the head of the corner.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the tenants and say what Jesus said about the rejected stone?
ev: Say what the tenants did to the servants and the son and what Jesus said about the stone.

nodes.t: David's Lord and Beware the Scribes
nodes.d: Jesus asks how Christ can be David's son when David calls him Lord in the Psalms, and warns the disciples about scribes who love long robes and best seats and devour widows' houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about David calling Christ Lord and his warning about scribes?
ev: Say the question Jesus asks about David and what he warns about the scribes.

nodes.t: Jesus Dies and Is Buried
nodes.d: Darkness falls, the temple veil is torn, Jesus cries 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit' and dies; the centurion glorifies God, and Joseph of Arimathaea lays the body in a new rock tomb as the women watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the death of Jesus and his burial?
ev: Say what signs and words marked Jesus' death and who buried him.

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.t: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
nodes.d: At Passover Jesus drives the sellers and money-changers out of the temple; asked for a sign, he says 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up', which John says he spoke of the temple of his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he meant by raising the temple in three days?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what sign he named and what John says it meant.

nodes.t: I Am the Bread of Life
nodes.d: The crowd seeks Jesus for the loaves; he says to labour for food that endures, that believing is the work of God, that Moses did not give the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life; all the Father gives him will come and he will raise them at the last day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by 'I am the bread of life' in this passage?
ev: Say what Jesus says he is and what he promises those who come to him.

nodes.t: I and My Father Are One
nodes.d: At the feast of dedication the Jews ask Jesus to say plainly if he is the Christ; he says his sheep hear his voice and no one can pluck them from his hand and 'I and my Father are one', and they take up stones, but he escapes beyond Jordan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about his sheep and his oneness with the Father?
ev: Say what Jesus says about his sheep and about himself and the Father.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: The crowd takes palm branches and cries 'Hosanna', Jesus rides a young donkey as written, the disciples later remember this after he is glorified, and the Pharisees say the world has gone after him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry into Jerusalem in John?
ev: Say how the crowd greeted Jesus and what John says the disciples understood later.

nodes.t: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
nodes.d: Before the Passover, knowing his hour has come, Jesus rises from supper and washes his disciples' feet; he says Peter will know later and that those he washes are clean, then tells them to wash one another's feet as he did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the foot washing and what Jesus said it was for?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what Peter said and what Jesus told the disciples to do.

nodes.t: The World's Hatred and the Witness of the Spirit
nodes.d: Jesus warns the disciples that the world hated him first and will hate them and persecute them, that the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, will testify of him, and that they will also bear witness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the world hates the disciples and who will bear witness according to Jesus?
ev: Say why Jesus says the world will hate his disciples and who will testify.

nodes.t: The Crucifixion
nodes.d: Jesus carries his cross to Golgotha and is crucified between two others under a title 'Jesus of Nazareth the King of the Jews'; soldiers cast lots for his coat, he commits his mother to the beloved disciple, says 'I thirst' and 'It is finished', bows his head and gives up the ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the crucifixion in John and name Jesus' last words?
ev: Say what Jesus said from the cross and what the soldiers did with his clothes.

nodes.t: Acts: overview
nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.t: Matthias takes the place of Judas
nodes.d: Peter says the scripture about Judas had to be fulfilled and that a witness of the resurrection must replace him. The group prays and the lot falls on Matthias, who is numbered with the eleven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the believers chose a replacement for Judas and how they chose him?
ev: State the requirement Peter gives for the one to be chosen (1:21-22)
Explain how Matthias was chosen (1:23-26)

nodes.t: Peter preaches at Pentecost
nodes.d: Peter says the outpouring is what Joel spoke of, declares that God raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ, and calls on the hearers to repent and be baptized. About three thousand are added that day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Peter's argument at Pentecost and what he told the people to do?
ev: Say how Peter uses Joel, and the Psalms of David, to explain Jesus (2:16-21, 2:25-35)
State what Peter tells the crowd to do and to whom the promise belongs (2:38-39)

nodes.t: Peter and John before the council
nodes.d: The priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees arrest Peter and John, and about five thousand have believed. Filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter tells the rulers there is salvation in no other name than Jesus, and when ordered to stop speaking they answer that they cannot but speak what they have seen and heard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said to the rulers and why he and John would not stop preaching?
ev: State what Peter says about the name of Jesus (4:10-12)
Explain how Peter and John answered the order to stop (4:19-20)

nodes.t: The church prays for boldness
nodes.d: Released, Peter and John report to their own company, and together they pray to God the maker of heaven and earth, recalling that rulers gathered against his Christ according to his counsel. They ask for boldness, the place is shaken, and they are filled with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the church prayed for after the threats and what happened next?
ev: Say what the believers asked God for (4:29-30)
Describe how God answered (4:31)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch
nodes.d: Invited to speak after the reading of the law and prophets, Paul traces Israel's story from Egypt through the judges and David to Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He declares forgiveness of sins and that by Jesus all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Paul's sermon from Israel's history to forgiveness through Jesus?
ev: Outline the history Paul recounts to reach Jesus (13:17-23)
State what Paul says is preached through Jesus (13:38-39)

nodes.t: Romans: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.t: All have sinned
nodes.d: Paul gathers Old Testament testimony to show that all are under sin and that no one is justified by the works of the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says every mouth is stopped (3:19)?
ev: State the conclusion of 3:19-20
Quote or paraphrase 3:23

nodes.t: Abraham justified by faith
nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham to show that righteousness is counted to the one who believes, before circumcision, and that Abraham is the father of all who believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 4 uses Genesis 15:6?
ev: Link Romans 4:3 to Genesis 15:6
Explain why it matters that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision (4:9-12)

nodes.t: Nothing can separate us from the love of God
nodes.d: Paul concludes that nothing in creation can separate believers from the love of God in Christ Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the end of Romans 8?
ev: Read 8:38-39 and list what Paul says cannot separate us

nodes.t: Faith comes by hearing
nodes.d: Righteousness is for everyone who believes; faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 10:9-10 and 10:17?
ev: State 10:9-10
Explain 10:17

nodes.t: The remnant and the olive tree
nodes.d: God has not cast off his people; a remnant is saved by grace, and Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the olive tree picture in Romans 11?
ev: Explain the olive tree illustration in 11:17-24
Say how the chapter ends (11:33-36)

nodes.t: The strong and the weak
nodes.d: Believers are to welcome one another, not judge over disputable matters, and seek the good of their neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says to treat a brother who disagrees on disputable matters?
ev: Explain 14:1 and 14:17

nodes.t: 1 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: Servants, builders and God's temple
nodes.d: Paul tells the divided Corinthians that he and Apollos are only servants, that God gives the increase, that Jesus Christ is the one foundation, and that the church is God's temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who gives growth in the church and what the foundation is, using 1 Corinthians 3?
ev: Explain the picture of planting and watering (3:6-7)
Say what the one foundation is (3:11)
Explain what happens to each builder's work (3:12-15)
Say why the church is called God's temple (3:16-17)

nodes.t: Liberty, conscience and the glory of God
nodes.d: Paul gives practical rules for eating what is sold in the market or served at a feast, tells believers to seek the good of others, and sums up: do all to the glory of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} apply 1 Corinthians 10:31 to an everyday choice and explain how seeking another's good fits with it?
ev: State the rule of 10:31
Explain what to do when someone says the food was offered to idols (10:28-29)
Say whom Paul asks them to follow (11:1)

nodes.t: If Christ is not raised: the firstfruits
nodes.d: Paul argues that if there is no resurrection of the dead then Christ is not risen and faith is vain, but Christ is risen as the firstfruits, as Adam brought death and Christ brings life, until death is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the resurrection of Christ matters for the believer, using 1 Corinthians 15:12-22?
ev: List the consequences if Christ is not risen (15:14-19)
Explain Adam and Christ in 15:21-22
Say what the last enemy is (15:26)

nodes.t: Ephesians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.t: Paul's prayer: Christ above all, head of the church
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks and prays that the Ephesians may know the hope of God's calling and the greatness of his power, which raised Christ and set him far above every power as head over all things to the church, his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about Christ's position and the church in Ephesians 1:20-23?
ev: Say what Paul prays that they may know (1:17-19)
Describe where God has set Christ (1:20-22)
Say what the church is to Christ (1:22-23)

nodes.t: Unity of the body and gifts for building up
nodes.d: Paul urges the Ephesians to walk worthy and keep the unity of the Spirit, lists the "one" things of the faith, and says the ascended Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to equip the saints and build up the body until it is mature.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Christ gave pastors and teachers to the church, using Ephesians 4:11-16?
ev: List the sevenfold unity of 4:4-6
Name the gifts given in 4:11
Say what the gifts are for (4:12-16)

nodes.t: God has spoken by his Son
nodes.d: God who spoke by the prophets has in these last days spoken by his Son, heir of all things, maker of the worlds, radiance of his glory, who purged sins and sat at God's right hand, better than the angels.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 1:1-4 says about how God has spoken and who the Son is?
ev: List what 1:2-3 says about the Son
Say how 1:4-14 compares him with angels

nodes.t: Jesus made like his brothers
nodes.d: Jesus, made a little lower than the angels, tasted death for everyone, shared flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free those enslaved by fear of death, and became a merciful and faithful high priest able to help the tempted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus became like his brothers according to Hebrews 2:14-18?
ev: Say why he shared flesh and blood (2:14-15)
State what kind of high priest he is (2:17)

nodes.t: Do not harden your hearts as in the wilderness
nodes.d: Quoting the warning that God swore the generation that provoked him in the wilderness would not enter his rest, the writer urges them to beware an evil heart of unbelief and to exhort one another daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to those who came out of Egypt and what warning the writer draws (3:16-19)?
ev: Say why that generation could not enter (3:19)
Describe what 3:12-13 tells the readers to do

nodes.t: A rest remains for the people of God
nodes.d: The promise of entering God's rest still stands: the gospel preached to them did not profit those without faith, God rested on the seventh day, and a Sabbath rest remains for God's people, so they must labour to enter it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the rest is that remains for God's people, and what warning goes with it (4:9-11)?
ev: Cite the creation rest mentioned in 4:4
State what remains for the people of God (4:9)
Say what the word of God does in 4:12

nodes.t: Called as high priest after Melchizedek's order
